text: Under which emperor did Sejanus rise to extraordinary influence?
What office made Sejanus one of the most powerful men in Rome?
Sejanus is most closely associated with which imperial military body?
What was the name of Sejanus's father, himself an equestrian official?
Before Sejanus held the prefecture alone, with whom had he shared command of the Guard?
Sejanus belonged to which social order rather than the senatorial class by birth?
What major reform of the Praetorian Guard is commonly credited to Sejanus?
choices: Stationing the cohorts together in one camp near Rome
Putting the Guard under senatorial command

text: The permanent camp built for the Praetorians under Tiberius was known by what name?
Concentrating the Praetorian Guard in a single camp had what immediate political effect?
choices: It reduced the Guard's visibility in Rome
It increased the Guard's cohesion and influence
It transferred command to the consuls
It made the Guard a provincial force

text: Which member of Tiberius's family died in 23 CE, opening more room for Sejanus's ambitions?
Ancient sources notoriously suggest that Sejanus helped remove Drusus the Younger through whom?
Livilla, linked in the sources with Sejanus, was the wife of which man?
Sejanus sought marriage into the imperial family by asking to marry whom?
Who refused Sejanus's request to marry Livilla?
What move by Tiberius in 26 CE helped Sejanus dominate politics at Rome more directly?
After Tiberius withdrew from Rome, Sejanus acted increasingly as what kind of figure?
Which imperial island residence is central to Sejanus's years of ascendancy?
The downfall of Agrippina the Elder and her sons is often connected with the influence of whom?
Which widow of Germanicus became a chief dynastic obstacle to Sejanus?
Which son of Germanicus was targeted early in the struggle surrounding Sejanus?
Which other son of Germanicus was later ruined amid the same campaign of court intrigue?
What legal climate of Tiberius's reign provided a weapon for Sejanus against opponents?
Roman charges of maiestas in this period are usually translated how?
Sejanus's political power depended especially on controlling access to which absent ruler?
What office did Sejanus hold jointly with Tiberius in 31 CE, signaling exceptional favor?
Which year saw both the peak of Sejanus's honors and his sudden destruction?
Who replaced Sejanus as the key security figure after his fall and later helped Caligula's succession?
Sejanus was destroyed after Tiberius sent what to the Senate?
Where was Sejanus arrested once Tiberius's message was read?
choices: In the Temple of Mars Ultor

text: What happened to Sejanus on the day of his downfall?
After Sejanus's execution, his body was reportedly subjected to what public indignity?
choices: Burial in the Mausoleum of Augustus

text: What sanction commonly followed the condemnation of Sejanus and his memory?
Which elderly matron is often credited in the sources with warning Tiberius against Sejanus?
Whose surviving son ultimately benefited most from Sejanus's elimination?
The future emperor Caligula was more formally known by what personal name?
Which grandson of Tiberius remained another dynastic possibility after Sejanus's fall?
Ancient historians often portray Sejanus as aspiring to what ultimate position?
What made Sejanus's apparent ambition especially alarming in Roman political terms?
choices: He was an equestrian reaching toward dynastic power

text: Which historian offers the most famous dark, psychological narrative of Sejanus's rise and fall?
Which biographer, rather than annalistic historian, also preserves lurid material about Tiberius and Sejanus?
Which contemporary author stands out for praising Sejanus and Tiberius rather than condemning them?
Velleius Paterculus's favorable portrait of Sejanus is often explained partly by what?
choices: His proximity to the regime while Sejanus was powerful

text: Which later senator-historian is another major narrative source for Sejanus besides Tacitus?
A recurrent modern caution about Sejanus is that our main literary sources are shaped by what?
What does Sejanus's career most clearly reveal about the early principate?
choices: That control of imperial access could rival formal office
That the Senate commanded the army

text: Which emperor had originally created the Praetorian Guard before Sejanus transformed its political weight?
Before Sejanus centralized them, the Praetorian cohorts had generally been what around Rome?
Why did centralizing the Guard near Rome matter so much constitutionally?
choices: It placed a concentrated armed force close to political institutions
It moved the army farther from the emperor

text: What kind of troops were the Praetorians in contrast to the frontier legions?
Sejanus's influence was strongest in Rome because Tiberius increasingly governed from where?
Which woman, mother of Tiberius, died in 29 CE and may have removed one restraint on factional struggle?
The death of Livia mattered for Sejanus's moment because she had represented what at court?
choices: An alternative center of Julio-Claudian prestige

text: Which imperial prince had died in 19 CE, leaving Agrippina's branch politically vulnerable but still symbolically potent?
choices: Nero Caesar the adopted son of Augustus

text: Sejanus's campaign against Agrippina's family was fundamentally a struggle over what?
Which body formally voted honors to Sejanus during his ascent?
Why is Sejanus often treated as a case study in the danger of imperial favorites?
choices: He turned delegated trust into personal domination

text: Which phrase best describes Tiberius's relationship to Sejanus before 31 CE?
The prefecture held by Sejanus was unusual because its commander answered directly to whom?
When Sejanus fell, the Praetorian Guard did not save him largely because control of the Guard had shifted to whom?
What is the best explanation for why Tiberius used a letter rather than appearing in person against Sejanus?
choices: He was campaigning on the Rhine
He remained absent on Capri and acted through written command

text: Which institution became a theater for terror after Sejanus's fall as accusations widened?
The purge after Sejanus's execution struck not only him but also what broader circle?
choices: Only members of the urban cohorts

text: Which of Sejanus's relatives, an uncle and distinguished general, was also caught in the aftermath?
What role did delatores play in the world Sejanus exploited?
choices: They acted as informers and prosecutors

text: Which feature of Tiberian government made delatores particularly feared?
choices: The use of political trials to test loyalty

text: Which son of Sejanus was executed in the purge after his father's fall?
Why did Sejanus's social origins matter less than his office while he was rising?
choices: Command of the Guard and imperial confidence outweighed pedigree
Only senators could hold the post

text: What did Sejanus's consulship in 31 CE imply to alarm contemporaries?
choices: That he intended to retire honorably
That an equestrian favorite was nearing dynastic legitimacy
That the Guard would be abolished
That Tiberius would return to republican elections

text: Which historian is especially skeptical about taking Tacitus's account of Tiberian motives at face value?
A major source problem in reconstructing Sejanus is that the surviving narratives were written when?
What might a revisionist interpretation of Sejanus emphasize more than the traditional villain portrait?
Even a revisionist reading usually concedes that Sejanus did help reshape which institution's political centrality?
Which later emperor's accession dramatically showed the Praetorian Guard could make and unmake rulers?
In retrospect, Sejanus's camp reform is important because it foreshadowed what later development?
choices: The end of all palace politics
A guard politics centered on Rome itself
The replacement of emperors by consuls

text: What most distinguishes the Praetorian prefecture from an ordinary republican magistracy?
choices: It derived from imperial appointment, not popular election

text: Which phrase best captures Sejanus's constitutional position?
choices: A powerful subordinate in an opaque monarchy
A provincial satrap independent of Rome

text: Why did rumors matter so much in Sejanus's Rome?
choices: Distance from the emperor made informal information politically potent
No one could meet in the Senate

text: What was the relationship between Sejanus and Tiberius's heir-problem in the 20s CE?
choices: It had no connection at all
His power grew as the succession became more uncertain
He solved it by adopting Claudius
He eliminated all Julio-Claudians by 25 CE

text: Sejanus's enemies could exploit what key weakness in his position?
choices: He lacked independent legitimacy once imperial favor vanished
He held tribunician power for life

text: Why was the Senate able to turn on Sejanus so abruptly?
choices: It had always been militarily stronger than the Guard
Its support for him depended on reading the emperor's wishes
It loved Agrippina the Elder unconditionally

text: What does Sejanus's sudden collapse suggest about autocracy under the early principate?
choices: Power could be immense yet instantly revocable
The emperor was legally constrained by juries

text: Which prince, son of Drusus the Younger, was sometimes viewed as a potential heir during Sejanus's period?
How did Sejanus's career affect the image of Tiberius in later historiography?
choices: It made him universally admired as transparent
It reinforced portrayals of suspicion, isolation, and cruelty
It turned him into a republican martyr
It detached him from all court politics

text: Which earlier death had already complicated Tiberian succession politics before Sejanus's climax?
Which of these was not a direct source of Sejanus's strength?
choices: Dynastic blood as a Julio-Claudian prince

text: What institutional lesson did later Romans draw from the Sejanus affair?
choices: A prefect with concentrated military access could threaten the regime
The Senate should command the frontiers directly
Emperors should always reside in Greece

text: Why is the Sejanus episode central to understanding the Julio-Claudian court?
choices: It was mainly a foreign war narrative
It shows how family, office, rumor, and force intertwined
It proves succession was always legally fixed
It has little to do with dynastic politics

text: Which emperor's personal withdrawal most enabled the emergence of a figure like Sejanus?
What basic contradiction of the principate did Sejanus exploit?
choices: That monarchy existed without openly naming itself monarchy
That senators could not hold office
That emperors were elected by women

text: When modern historians debate whether Sejanus planned a coup, what is usually the main issue?
choices: Whether he ever lived in Rome
How literally to trust hostile literary narratives

text: Which of these best reflects a cautious modern judgment about Sejanus?
choices: He was certainly an innocent victim
He was certainly emperor in all but name
He was exceptionally powerful, but his exact aims remain uncertain

text: What did the destruction of Sejanus fail to do in the long run?
choices: Remove the Praetorian Guard from politics

text: Which phrase best describes the Praetorian Guard after Sejanus's reforms?
choices: A ceremonial escort with no command structure
A concentrated imperial force with urban political leverage
A provincial militia recruited in Syria
A senatorial honor guard without weapons

text: What personal quality do ancient authors repeatedly attribute to Sejanus, whether fairly or not?
Which of these developments would most have signaled to contemporaries that Sejanus was nearing the center of power?
choices: Consular honors and a marriage bid into the imperial family
Election as tribune of the plebs
Command of the Alexandrian grain fleet

text: What role did fear play in Sejanus's political system as portrayed by Tacitus?
choices: It disciplined elites and distorted normal deliberation
It mattered only in the provinces

text: Which of these best captures why Sejanus remains historically important?
choices: He exposed how dependent early empire was on proximity, personnel, and armed loyalty
He wrote the legal code of Rome
